stories.headline: How Jackson Chourio became a Brewers superstar in October
stories.summary: After a four-hit Game 3, Chourio is setting a new standard for young players in October.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Jackson Chourio is 22 years old.

"A kid," as Milwaukee Brewers hitting coach Daniel Vogelbach put it late Monday night. "He could be playing college baseball right now."

Instead, Game 3 of the World Series -- a 10-1 thrashing of the Tampa Bay Rays that saw Chourio collect a quarter of the Brewers' 16 hits -- was Chourio's 23rd career postseason game, all in these past three years. Through them, he has built a catalogue of experience in his sport's most pressure-packed environments, steeling himself to the point that he has mastered them.

"It's about maintaining a calmness to myself and thinking only about a positive result," Chourio said in Spanish. "I know people expect a lot out of me. I expect a lot out of myself too. But I have to remain calm and always think positive."

On a night when the Brewers put themselves up 3-0 and on the precipice of the first championship in the franchise's 57-year history, Chourio became the first 22-year-old in 80 years to accumulate four hits in a World Series game.

He has collected eight of them across the first three games of the Series, during which the Brewers' offense has put its relentlessness on display -- by blitzing Nick Martinez in the first inning of Game 1, by overcoming a four-run deficit in Game 2 and by stringing together eight two-out runs in the fifth inning of Game 3.

Chourio started Monday's rally with a base hit up the middle and finished it with a double into the right-center-field gap, because of course he did.

"He's turning into a superstar right in front of our eyes," Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said.

Arnold was the general manager under David Stearns when the Brewers signed Chourio out of Venezuela as a 16-year-old in 2021. The efficient swing and the lightning-fast hands were immediately obvious. Over time, Chourio's ability to unleash those traits on baseball's grandest stage became apparent too, to the point where, as Brewers right fielder Sal Frelick said, these types of performances are now expected of him.

"He's got that slow heartbeat," Brewers captain Christian Yelich said of Chourio. "He likes the moment."

A multihit performance in Chourio's postseason debut in 2024 and a .389/.421/.667 slash line in his first National League Division Series in 2025 have given way to an entire month of brilliance in 2026. It began subtly, with the poise to calmly catch a Ty France fly ball that clanked off a roof cable in Game 1 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres, and continued with an epic walk-off single against star closer Mason Miller 24 hours later.

After that, Néstor Corredor -- the Brewers field coordinator who also coached Chourio in the Venezuelan winter league and in this year's World Baseball Classic -- noticed Chourio getting too anxious, especially in the NL Championship Series rematch against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Corredor has since seen Chourio dial back in -- working counts, shortening his swing, slowly dismantling the Rays with an assortment of low line drives.

The success of those around Chourio has helped.

"He's understanding that this is a complete team and he doesn't have to be the hero," Corredor said. "He's the leader of the lineup, but there's a calmness to him, knowing that there's a team behind him to support him."

Over the past three years, the league's OPS is 39 points higher in the regular season than it is in the postseason. For Chourio, it's the opposite. His regular-season OPS from 2024 to 2026 -- during which he became the first player with three consecutive 20-homer, 20-steal seasons before the age of 23 -- is .799. In the playoffs, it's .882.

"It's super impressive how he manages that scenario," Brewers backup catcher Gary Sánchez said in Spanish. "To me, he likes these moments more than the regular season."

Chourio adamantly believes he was born to perform in this environment.

Perhaps his name has something to do with it.

Chourio's father, Jackson Sr., was a die-hard Los Angeles Lakers fan during their dominant run in the early 2000s. Chourio's younger brother, Jaison, an outfielder in the Cleveland Guardians system, has the middle name "Oneel" in honor of Shaquille O'Neal. Chourio's middle name is "Bryan," a nod to the late Kobe Bryant. Chourio isn't fluent in English, but he said he has read some of Bryant's autobiography, "The Mamba Mentality," and has tried to adopt what he can from the Lakers' playoff legend.

There's a key difference, though: Bryant famously shot air balls in his first exposure to the playoffs. He had to work himself into becoming the five-time champion who built a legacy off thriving in the biggest moments.

Chourio got there really early.

"I know how hard I've worked for this," he said. "But the fact it's all working out the best way possible is truly gratifying."

stories.headline: Bafana boss Pitso Mosimane's latest South Africa squad shows favouritism fears were unfounded
stories.summary: Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.
stories.body:
When Pitso Mosimane returned as Bafana Bafana head coach, sceptics feared that his proximity to South African club football would lead to an erosion of the meritocratic culture Hugo Broos had built, but the 62-year-old's second preliminary squad suggests it has only been enhanced.

Mosimane began his tenure with Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying wins over Guinea and Eritrea and a friendly victory over Egypt. Next up is the AFCON qualifying double-header against Kenya on Nov. 13 & 17.

Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.

Chicago Fire's Mbekezeli Mbokazi has returned from injury, while Aden McCarthy, Botiumelo Radiopane, Nqaba Xulu, Luke le Roux, Thalente Mbatha, Nkosikhona Radebe, Devin Titus and Thakasani Mbanjwa have also received call-ups.

For every one of these call-ups, a layman can deduce a clear possible motive. McCarthy is the most obvious among them -- he has consistently featured at centre-back for Sabah in the UEFA Champions League and performed well at the highest level.

Radiopane and Xulu are in hot scoring form domestically for Orlando Pirates and Richards Bay respectively. Titus has earned his place with a strong start to life at MAS Fes in Morocco. Mbatha is back from injury and le Roux on the books of a new club at Cercle Brugge after struggling for game time at Portsmouth.

Radebe adds a right-back option from an in-form AmaZulu side with Mamelodi Sundowns' Khuliso Mudau still on the mend from injury. Mbanjwa is rewarded for a strong start to the season in goal for Golden Arrows.

Yanela Mbuthuma and Shandre Campbell -- both of whom have experienced dips in form and fortune at club level since the last international break -- are notable absentees.

In cutting two players he had given opportunities to after they had been mostly overlooked by Broos, Mosimane suggested he is willing to operate without fear or favour.

When 'Jingles' was on the verge of being appointed, Broos was quoted as telling Het Nieuwsblad: "You know, South Africa still don't have a coach. The candidate is Pitso Mosimane, a successful South African coach.

"But they know that if he comes in, they'll go five years back in time. Club owners and agents calling coaches to influence the squad selection. I threw all of them out. If one called, I would say bluntly: 'I don't talk with agents'."

The concern over agents and owners trying their luck in influencing the Bafana head coach may have been well-founded. Broos was not the first to complain of this within the national team setup.

However, questioning if Mosimane himself was open to influence without proof he was willing to make publicly available was ill-advised. It is impossible to accurately speculate on what conversations have or have not gone on between Mosimane and club owners and agents in the two months since then, but what is clear is that his team selection has been thoroughly meritocratic.

The momentum he has garnered is reminiscent of what Broos achieved in the first six months of his tenure.

At the time, the Belgian's irreverent team selection and approach to squad culture put everybody on their toes and led to an uptick in results. After they had failed to qualify for AFCON 2021 immediately before Broos was appointed, the Belgian fell narrowly short of steering Bafana into qualification playoffs for the 2022 World Cup.

In subsequent years, he kicked on and led Bafana to third place at AFCON 2023 (held belatedly in Ivory Coast in early 2024) and the 2026 World Cup round of 32.

When discussing the most successful Bafana Bafana coaches of all-time, Broos should be placed alongside Clive Barker in the top two. However, even the brightest tacticians eventually settle on patterns in their squad selection, and towards the end of his tenure, the Belgian became more predictable in certain aspects.

There was a fairly settled back five of Ronwen Williams, Aubrey Modiba, Mbokazi, Ime Okon and Mudau, and until he switched up his attacking plan to revive the FIFA World Cup campaign, Broos was likely to start Lyle Foster upfront with Evidence Makgopa the main alternative.

In midfield, Teboho Mokoena was a near certain starter and Sphephelo Sithole the clear preferred option alongside him, although Broos occasionally tinkered with his formation and left room for the likes of Bathusi Aubaas and the late Jayden Adams in the holding role. Nkosinathi Sibisi was considered another option, occasionally stepping out from the back into midfield.

Mosimane's arrival has reopened competition for places in these positions. Brooklyn Poggenpoel is retained in the squad after impressing in midfield over the last international break.

After Mbuthuma's minutes upfront, Radiopane and Xulu have been given a chance to earn theirs. Foster has made a second successive preliminary squad, although he failed to make the final squad last time out while in the process of leaving Burnley on loan to Houston Dynamo and settling in.

Fawaaz Basadien, Olwethu Makhanya, and McCarthy are in consideration in the backline. Mudau is, however, still the likely first-choice at right-back for the time being when he returns to full fitness. Still, Mosimane has done well to identify alternatives.

Mosimane declined to get drawn into a war of words with Broos over anything not directly related to matters on the pitch and instead praised his predecessor's impressive record as Bafana head coach.

In his first stint, Mosimane may not have succeeded in the hotseat. However, early results and his approach to team selection suggest he has justified the decision of the South African Football Association (SAFA) to give him a second chance and trust him to navigate the role without fear or favour to anyone.

stories.headline: Cowboys keep pace in NFC East, end 2-game slide with road win over Eagles
stories.summary: Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, and the Cowboys averted a three-game losing streak to keep pace in the NFC East with a 38-21 win over the Eagles.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott has been around long enough to know there was added importance to Monday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Having lost two straight to fall to 2-4, Prescott helped make sure the streak ended, throwing three touchdown passes in the Cowboys' 38-21 win.

The Cowboys averted a three-game losing streak, kept pace with the 4-2-1 New York Giants in the NFC East and at least temporarily interrupted the unease that was developing around the team.

"We say the division's right in front of us. It is as long as we win," Prescott said. "And if you lose another game, then you're probably checking to see what New York's doing. You're probably checking and watching the other teams more than we should. So yeah, I mean you got to win games, got to win division games. How big of a game this was, understanding how much they're hurt on their offensive side, yeah, huge road win for us."

With their defense raising concerns all season, the Cowboys entered Monday facing questions about an offense that scored a combined 29 points in its past two games. Prescott threw four interceptions in those games, while head coach and playcaller Brian Schottenheimer received outside pressure after he said during the week, "I know how great of a coach I am," despite a 9-13-1 record, and that he is an "elite playcaller" on 105.3 The Fan despite the recent woes.

Though Schottenheimer had his normal postgame celebration inside the locker room with the players Monday night, highlighting key plays offensively and defensively, he was unusually reserved in his postgame comments.

"Had nothing to do with desperation," Schottenheimer said. "Our guys just played good."

Asked why he wasn't as exuberant after a win and if he was OK, Schottenheimer said, "I'm great. Excited for our guys."

Though Prescott said he did not discuss the criticism with Schottenheimer, Prescott said he noticed a "definitely hungry, pissed-off version of Schotty."

"It's not like he's naive," Prescott said. "It's not like he hadn't heard some noise about him and whether it's the call in the games or whatever doubt that's been out there. But we've got his back. He knows that. He's a guy that takes a lot of pride in his job, a lot of pride in his team. Everybody handles everything different, so I don't blame him to an extent. We've got his back. More importantly, it's just about us going out there and executing on Sundays."

For the first time since 1983, the Cowboys had more than 200 yards rushing and 200 yards passing against the Eagles. Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards on 25 carries, scoring the game-sealing final touchdown from 2 yards out with 2:21 to play.

Prescott had his sixth career game of at least three passing touchdowns against the Eagles. He threw two to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens.

Defensively, the Cowboys allowed the Eagles' first touchdown of the opening possession and first touchdown on the opening possession of the second half but did enough to help. The Cowboys picked off one of Tanner McKee's passes (DeMarvion Overshown) and sacked him twice (Quinnen Williams, Donovan Ezeiruaku).

"We didn't put together a perfect game," Williams said. "We've got to learn from it. But it's amazing to get a win."

Only 22 days had passed since the Cowboys' last win -- Oct. 4 at the Houston Texans -- but Dallas needed this victory against a team that was struggling even more. The Cowboys next face the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Dallas has not won back-to-back games since a three-game winning streak in Weeks 11-13 last year.

"Nobody's going to give it to us. Nobody's going to say, 'Yeah, you're the better team. You got it,'" Prescott said. "That's what's so great about the NFL, so we've got to come out and earn it each and every week, and there's going to be no difference coming next Sunday."

With the win, the Cowboys have a 57% chance of winning the division, according to ESPN Analytics.

Said Schottenheimer: "I think it gets us right back into the hunt in the NFC East."

stories.headline: Smesko rips refs for 'ridiculous' missed calls on Reese in Game 5 of WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Dream head coach Karl Smesko blasted refs for missing what he called a "ridiculous" amount of contact on Angel Reese in Monday night's Game 5 loss.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Atlanta Dream coach Karl Smesko stood defiantly behind star Angel Reese on Monday night, criticizing officials for missing what he called a "ridiculous" amount of contact in Monday night's 64-55 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 5 of the WNBA Finals.

Reese finished with seven points on 2-of-8 shooting and went 3-of-4 from the free throw line in the loss, which put Atlanta in a 3-2 series hole.

"I give [the Valkyries] credit for playing good defense, they're known for their defense," Smesko said. "But I want to have Angel's back here. The contact on Angel compared to everybody else is just ridiculous. Just ridiculous."

He added about the officiating: "You can't be at this level and make that many mistakes."

Smesko's main point of contention was what he felt to be a number of missed calls against Reese. He also said he felt there were a number of missed double dribbles and travel calls against the Valkyries.

Reese shared in the frustration, saying the physical play and questionable officiating have been a recurring theme for her this year.

"I am still trying to figure out how to play through the physicality," said Reese, who was also called for four personal fouls. "I'm kind of used to it because this was happening throughout the season, so I have to just continue to play through it. But honestly, for my teammates, when they're getting slapped to the floor or knocked off, it's a little frustrating."

She continued: "I know I have the mismatch, especially talking about matchups. So when I do switch on the post and I'm a lot stronger than the opponent, I should be able to turn and they're calling an offensive foul. But when I'm getting pushed before that, it's frustrating to me."

It's the first time in Reese's career she has had consecutive games with two or fewer field goals, in the regular season or postseason, and just the second time she has been held to single-digit scoring in consecutive games (2024).

In Game 4, Reese had eight points on 2-of-12 shooting and hit four of her six attempted free throws. She was also called for four fouls in that game.

Reese said she felt a shift in officiating in Game 4.

Atlanta took 116 free throws in the first four games (29.0 per game). In Games 2, 3 and 4, the Dream became the second team to attempt at least 25 free throws in three straight Finals games in WNBA history, according to ESPN Insights.

As a team, the Dream shot 11-of-14 from the free throw line Monday, the fewest free throw attempts they've had in a game this postseason. It's tied for their second fewest in any game this season.

"It definitely shifted when we went up 2-1," Reese said. "I don't know what happened, but it definitely took a big turn."

Overall, Game 5 was a historically bad scoring night for both teams. The Valkyries' 64 points were the fewest in a Finals win since the Sacramento Monarchs in 2005, and the Dream's 55 were the fewest in a Finals game since the Mercury in Game 3 of the 2021 Finals.

Atlanta hit just 29.2% of their shots, the fourth lowest by any team in a WNBA Finals game, and just 23.5% in the paint, the worst by any team in a game this postseason.

"There are things that are on us, like we're missing shots we should make. But at the same time, that needs to be a whole lot better than it was," Smesko said. "It you push someone with two hands, that's got to be a foul. I'm kind of tired of some of the excuses that I'm hearing."

Meanwhile, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said this level of physicality is expected at this stage of the Finals and series.

"Both teams really want to win this," Nakase said. "These are two defensive-minded teams ... they like physicality, so that's part of it. I ain't shocked about this. You have an Atlanta Dream team that's well-coached, that have dogs, same as us."

stories.headline: Red Wings' Michal Postava a winner in first career NHL start
stories.summary: Michal Postava made his first career NHL start a memorable one, backstopping the Red Wings to a shootout win over the Oilers.
stories.body:
Michal Postava made his first career NHL start a memorable one Monday night.

Postava made 25 stops in regulation and three more in a shootout as the Detroit Red Wings beat Connor McDavid and the high-flying Oilers 4-3 in Edmonton, Alberta.

The 24-year-old undrafted netminder from Czechia was appearing in his second career game, after replacing John Gibson in the third period of a 5-2 win against Vancouver last Thursday.

"It's amazing," Postava told Detroit SportsNet. "It's a big win for me. I'm happy now that I help guys, and guys help me. Three times we were losing, and we still can get it, so it's a great win for us."

One of Postava's stops in the shootout came against McDavid.

"Crazy, he's like one of the best players that's ever played," Postava said. "I'm just happy. I don't have words."

Lucas Raymond scored the only goal of the shootout and had a pair of assists in regulation for Detroit. Viktor Arvidsson, Emmitt Finnie and Dylan Larkin added the goals in regulation for the Red Wings, who went 2-1-1 on a four-game road trip.

Detroit fell behind three times and tied the game for a third time with 1:17 remaining in the third period. With Postava pulled, a bouncing puck came to Larkin in front and he shoveled in his second of the season.

Vasily Podkolzin, Isaac Howard and Colton Dach scored for the Oilers, who have lost two straight as well as forward Zach Hyman to what looked to be a concussion.

McDavid had an assist to extend his season-starting points streak to 12 games, now with an NHL-best 34 points. He set a team record for most points before Nov. 1, and also matched the longest season-opening assist streak in NHL history, matching Sebastian Aho, Ken Linseman and Wayne Gretzky.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with his crowning moment
stories.summary: After a remarkable year for Bayern Munich and England, Harry Kane becoming the world's best player is the ultimate reward for years of perseverance.
stories.body:
LONDON -- It is nine years since Harry Kane lingered at the back of the London Palladium at the end of a soccer awards show.

The Best FIFA Football Awards in 2017 had just concluded with Cristiano Ronaldo handed the men's top prize in addition to leading a team of the year including Lionel Messi, Neymar, Sergio Ramos and Gianluigi Buffon.

As the audience filed out and a few mere mortals loitered in the hope of a selfie, Kane stood near the exit, casting a longing stare at the winners on stage. He has dreamed all his life of being in their place, considered in the same breath as the game's greats.

On Monday, at the same storied West End venue, about nine miles from his birthplace in Leytonstone, he finally is. Sat next to Lamine Yamal with last year's winner Rodri one place further away, Kane kept company with the elite. And then he joined them.

Last week in Munich, he told reporters he had found the wait to learn the winner "very stressful" for himself and his family. The final few hours on Monday won't have helped. The rain present earlier in the day subsided, but the controversy did not.

Less than three hours before the ceremony was due to start, the official website published a profile of Kane as the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner. Alongside one for Kylian Mbappé and one for Yamal. They were swiftly deleted. The entire ceremony was then delayed by 45 minutes with no official reason given, amid some speculation that the notorious London traffic was responsible.

Kane won on the undercard -- the Gerd Müller Men's Award or the Striker of the Year -- to cheers from the locals in the audience. The raucous reaction from the cheap seats before addressing the crowd was a prelude to what followed. It was palpably welcome but not, by itself, an indication of the big one: Striker of the Year is not decided by vote but simply by goals, and Kane's 73 was the best in the men's game.

Having waited for over a decade to live this moment, a few extra minutes made no difference in the end.

"Wow, wow, wow," he said after taking the stage before thanking Tottenham Hotspur by saying "I wouldn't be where I am without you" in a moment of typical class.

Monday's Ballon d'Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose story of relentless professionalism and determined aspiration serves as an exemplar for any young player. British media is often criticized for prematurely building up players to an impossible level, only to then knock them down when that level is inevitably never reached.

Kane has always been a different case. He publicly judged himself against Ronaldo and Messi, two of the best in history, and used their devastating consistency as a target to match.

His numbers since joining Bayern Munich are staggering: 158 goals in 156 matches following a €120 million move from Tottenham in 2023. The Ballon d'Or voting period takes into account August 2025 to the end of the World Cup in July.

He scored 73 goals in 65 matches during that period, won the Bundesliga, the DFB-Pokal, the German Supercup and led England to their best FIFA World Cup finish in 60 years with third place, scoring six times at the tournament.

Back in 2017, "The Best" awards were a competition set up by FIFA as a rival to the Ballon d'Or after five years of partnership with organizers France Football had come to an end. Kane was on the 24-man shortlist for Best Men's Player that year. He finished 24th. Of course, his journey to the summit began much further back.

Coming through the Spurs academy, a young Kane had loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City, where you would find it extremely difficult to locate anyone honest who genuinely believed at the time they were in the presence of a future world-class talent. A nice kid, sure, a hard worker with a future in the game. But one of England's greatest?

Kane broke into Spurs' first team toward the end of the 2013-14 season and a year later was named PFA Young Player of the Year aged 21, making his England debut in the same season. He marked that moment against Lithuania with a goal then, too.

Fame was a novelty at this point. During a Tottenham preseason tour to Sydney, Kane innocently ventured out to a shopping center in his downtime. He was quickly mobbed by so many adoring fans that the club had to scramble a minibus to bring him back to the team hotel.

Kane went on to score 280 goals in 435 appearances for Spurs while breaking Wayne Rooney's all-time goal-scoring record for England. Barring injury, he will break Peter Shilton's appearance record of 125 caps next month, too.

There was, though, perhaps a sense in the buildup that Kane was not quite the global superstar his Ballon d'Or rivals were, most obviously Messi and Mbappé but also, despite his teenage years, Yamal, named Young Talent of the Year for the third consecutive year.

Former Spurs boss Jose Mourinho alluded to this in a conversation with Kane captured by Amazon in their "All or Nothing" series covering the 2019-20 campaign.

"The world looks to English football with an incredible respect but they still think that the movie stars of football belong to other places -- and I think we have to build also your status in that direction," he said.

Kane replied: "That's my aim. When you are at a club like Tottenham, of course we've done well, personally I've done well, but I want to be Ronaldo, Messi ..."

There he goes again. The Ballon d'Or is voted for by one journalist per country of FIFA's top 100 ranked nations, which brings a different dynamic than, say, the FIFA equivalent, which adds votes from national managers and captains.

He had never finished higher than 10th in the Ballon d'Or vote (2024). There are three criteria, listed in order of importance: individual performances, decisive and impressive character; collective performances and titles won; class and fair play.

And despite the Premier League being one of the United Kingdom's most successful global exports, English players have only ever won it five times (Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan twice) and nobody has triumphed since Michael Owen in 2001.

That's more than two decades of unprecedented growth for the Premier League, and yet LaLiga often feels as though it is where the true individual talents reside. Players from Real Madrid and Barcelona have won it 12 times each. Manchester United are the most successful English club in Ballon d'Or history with four.

Kane, of course, left England in pursuit of silverware after a decade of personal achievement but collective frustration at Spurs. In doing so, he has ended up landing both silverware with Bayern and now the highest individual honor a player can attain.

"I am almost speechless," he said. "Being here in London has made it extra special. It made it a good omen for me tonight." Where once he stared at the Palladium stage, now all eyes are on him.

stories.headline: Manchester City charges: Features, explainers, what's next after guilty verdict
stories.summary: ESPN has you covered with everything you need to know about the latest in the Manchester City scandal.
stories.body:
After an investigation spanning years, Manchester City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. The decision is a major development in one of the biggest scandals in soccer history, but the saga is far from over.

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

O'Hanlon: Man City cheated because the Premier League's rules gave them no other choice
The Premier League is unfair: Some teams are allowed to spend more than everyone else. So, of course Man City cheated to win.

Tighe: Man City's alternate universe: Guardiola, Haaland to Arsenal? Arteta to PSG?
What would the sport have looked like if City had not spent in the way that they did? Who would have won the eight league titles? Where would the superstars (like Erling Haaland) they signed have gone instead? And what would manager Pep Guardiola's career have looked like without a decade-long stint in Manchester?

Lindop: Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?
Under Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola, Liverpool and Man City pushed the Premier League's standards higher than ever. But was it all a sham?

Dawson: 'We're Not Really Here': As Man City sanctions loom, it's the fans who suffer
Manchester City's financial malfeasance could send the club back down the football pyramid, a place where fans of a certain age are very familiar.

Olley: Arsenal fight back to win as Premier League resumes under cloud of Man City verdict
Does Arsenal's comeback win over Leeds close the gap on leaders Man City, or extend their own lead at the top? This is the perpetual uncertainty that hangs over the Premier League now.

Ogden: What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take
Man City have appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board also begins its work on figuring out appropriate punishments. So what happens next, and what is the possible timeline?

Marcotti: We don't get Man City guilty verdict without hacker Rui Pinto, but it doesn't make him a hero

stories.headline: Alexander Volkanovski could face a new challenge after UFC 333
stories.summary: Alexander Volkanovski and Petr Yan defended titles at UFC 333, but which champion could fight in a new division?
stories.body:
While both champions who topped the UFC 333 fight card successfully defended their belts, their next moves will likely be in different directions.

Featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski needed only two rounds to put away formerly unbeaten challenger Movsar Evloev. Now, he could try his luck again in the weight class that is home to two of his three UFC losses.

Meanwhile, men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan beat Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision to close his trilogy with the former titleholder. Yan could follow his trilogy bout with another rematch, as two possible challengers have already faced him in the Octagon -- including one who already holds a victory over Yan.

Let's take a look at the most likely scenarios and a wild card for Volkanovski, Yan and more winners and losers on the UFC 333 main card.

Alexander Volkanovski, featherweight champion
Who should be next: Charles Oliveira

If Oliveira successfully defends the BMF title against Diego Lopes at UFC 335 in December, this is the fight to make. Both are MMA legends, and neither has shown signs of falling off. Making this fight in 2027 wouldn't feel like an attempt to squeeze name value out of two fading fighters. It would feel as if it was happening right at the right time. The BMF angle doesn't add much for me, but if the UFC is going to keep that belt going, Volkanovski is more than qualified to fight for it. It would also give Volkanovski a chance to prove himself as a lightweight title contender. He told ESPN in September he didn't love the idea of jumping the line at lightweight to fight Justin Gaethje, especially with an obvious title challenger like Arman Tsarukyan. The BMF fight would legitimize the winner as a real challenger for the 155-pound belt.

Wild card: Tsarukyan

Gaethje hasn't said whether he intends to fight again. If he does, Tsarukyan is next. Gaethje has said he's next in line, and the UFC has told Tsarukyan he is. But if Gaethje decides to walk into the sunset after that White House win in June, there'd obviously be a vacant slot. Volkanovski deserves it. Send him straight into the title shot against Tsarukyan.

Movsar Evloev, featherweight
Who should be next: Pat Sabatini

I didn't love Evloev's choice of words, of "maybe I'll try again," regarding his future as a featherweight title challenger. Perhaps chalk that up to English being his second language. Hopefully, he won't be too discouraged by his first loss coming at the hands of the greatest 145-pounder ever. Regardless of his mindset, he is undeniably in a tough spot. It took him a long time to get to the top. It's probably a safe bet it will take him a while to get back. He will be in the position of gatekeeper for a minute. There's no other way to say it. The most obvious name in that group right now is Sabatini, who is 9-2 in the UFC.

Wild card: Steve Garcia

Garcia would be the second-most obvious name in that category, coming off a loss to Diego Lopes at UFC Freedom 250 in June.

Petr Yan, men's bantamweight champion

Who should be next: Sean O'Malley

Yan vs. O'Malley is the biggest fight available. Has O'Malley really earned a title shot? Since losing to Merab Dvalishvili in 2024 and 2025, he's only 2-0 -- with a close win over Song Yadong and a knockout of Aiemann Zahabi. Those two wins don't scream title shot, to be fair. But it's also impossible to strongly argue against O'Malley. He holds a victory (albeit a controversial one) over Yan from 2022. Beyond O'Malley, Song has the strongest case for a title shot -- and O'Malley just beat him in January. Even if you thought O'Malley lost to Yan back in 2022, it was a fantastic, competitive fight. We always knew the UFC would revisit it someday. I don't see why that day wouldn't be now.

Wild card: Song

If the UFC wants to give Yan this rematch instead, I'm in favor. It makes the most sense to go with O'Malley, but as a fight fan, I like the idea of Yan vs. Song, probably because of how Song knocked out Umar Nurmagomedov with one shot in the pocket. Yan vs. O'Malley would be an interesting chess match, but Song's firepower and speed are game changers. Yan will likely face both fighters eventually. O'Malley makes more sense to come first for a variety of reasons, but the more explosive matchup for Yan might be Song.

Merab Dvalishvili, men's bantamweight
Who should be next: Umar Nurmagomedov

I wouldn't expect Dvalishvili to sit on the sideline very long. He was just forced to wait 10 months for his trilogy bout with Yan, and now he's coming off the disappointment of his second loss in a row. I imagine he'll be eager to get back in the cage. The Nurmagomedov rematch is honestly a no-brainer. There's genuine heat between them. Nurmagomedov will presumably want to return by January, before he observes the Muslim holiday of Ramadan beginning in February. Their first fight was fight of the night at UFC 311 in January 2025. Nurmagomedov broke his hand early in that bout, and Dvalishvili later revealed he fought through injuries during camp. Now, both are coming off a loss, which the UFC loves to consider in matchmaking. There's a million reasons to run this one back, and I expect the UFC to do it.

Wild card: Payton Talbott

This makes sense for obvious reasons. It's a big jump in competition for Talbott, but he has earned the right to make it. Talbott has shown the kind of potential the UFC can -- and will -- reward with shortcuts. He doesn't need to beat Nos. 5 through 10 in the divisional rankings to earn a title shot. It still feels early for Talbott to make this sort of leap, but it's also the right moment to face a former champion. If Talbott loses, it's no big deal, because, at 28 years old, he still has plenty of time. If he wins, he becomes a legitimate title contender overnight.

Aaron Pico, featherweight

Who should be next: Jean Silva

I suggested this matchup after Pico's last win over Patricio Pitbull in April, and I see no reason not to double down. On paper, it's arguably the most explosive fight in the division -- especially with Diego Lopes moving to lightweight to fight Charles Oliveira in December. Silva would be a big jump up the rankings for Pico, but honestly, it's a bigger fight for Silva than most other potential top-10 matchups. Pico has always shown unmatched potential, but has fallen victim to devastating finishes throughout his career. This potential UFC Fight Night main event would be one of the scariest fights in the division for Pico. Let's see how he handles it.

Wild card: Youssef Zalal

Zalal, 30, has had an interesting career. He signed with the UFC in 2020 with a lot of hype, then went 0-3 and was cut in 2021. He fought his way back to the promotion and won five in a row before losing to Aljamain Sterling in April. A matchup against Pico would pit two featherweights against each other who have shown immense potential but haven't fully realized it.

stories.headline: Who I would -- and would not -- want to be this AFL offseason
stories.summary: The AFL offseason is in full swing but it won't stop us from analysing the landscape. Here's who Jake Michaels would (and wouldn't!) want to be heading into 2027.
stories.body:
From Brisbane's stunning three-peat to Fremantle's Grand Final capitulation, high-profile free agent signings to ongoing legal battles, so much has happened in the AFL world over the past month. So, who would you want to be (and not want to be) this off-season.

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Those I WOULD NOT want to be this AFL offseason
Ross Lyon
No coach will enter season 2027 under more scrutiny and pressure than Ross Lyon. St Kilda was widely tipped to rise up the ladder this season just gone after being the most active club during the previous trade and free agency period. Instead, the Saints severely underwhelmed, winning just 10 games and finishing a disappointing 11th on the ladder, 10 premiership points outside of the wildcard finals. The club is desperate to retain the services of superstar midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera, who is out of contract at season's end and could easily be tempted with a blockbuster move back to South Australia. As a result, St Kilda's powerbrokers likely won't tolerate another sluggish start, which means Lyon has absolutely zero margin for error in 2027.

Fremantle fans
Alright, alright, I'm sorry to bring it up again. And please feel free to skip ahead if you don't want to re-live it once more. But the reality is every single Dockers fan will be replaying those harrowing final four-and-a-bit minutes of the Grand Final in their mind all offseason, wondering how on earth their team coughed up what appeared to be an insurmountable late lead. The heartbreaking loss to Brisbane is as devastating as it gets for a footy club and you could almost understand if any Fremantle fan never wanted to watch the sport again. Seriously, I'm not sure how you ever get over that loss. It all just means the next five months are going to feel like an eternity.

Andrew McGrath
It was an incredibly disappointing season from new Essendon skipper Andrew McGrath, who averaged a career-low in disposals, kicked just two goals, and failed to poll a single Brownlow Medal vote. To be a captain of a club that won just two games for the entire year and still be unable to crack the top 10 of the best and fairest count is pretty embarrassing, really. With former skipper Zach Merrett now no longer at the club, McGrath, who has now been in the league for a decade and tallied 200 games, is Essendon's main man. It's time he starts to play like it or else he risks further damage to his reputation.

Chris Fagan's replacement
Whoever is entrusted with the task of succeeding Chris Fagan at the Lions will be feeling the pressure and the eyes of the footy world on them from day one. It's a bit like following Jerry Seinfeld on stage. How can you possibly back up that act!? Fagan completely revitalised Brisbane, leading the club out of the doldrums and to its second three-peat this century. And while Fagan's tenure is up and dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale has departed for Collingwood, nobody feels as if the Lions are over the hump. In fact, quite the contrary. The age profile of this list should have them contending for years to come. That can be both a blessing or a curse for any new coach.

The Pullman Five

Okay, this one might be a tad on the nose, but who would want to be one of Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice, or James Jordan this offseason? The incident at the Pullman Hotel in Melbourne on the eve of finals remains a legal matter, meaning there are still so many unknowns when it comes to the footballing careers of these five. Can Heeney and Warner ever ingratiate themselves to the Swans' faithful once more? Will Bice and Jordan be shuffled out of the best team? And then there's Blakey. North Melbourne gave up the farm for his signature and much will be expected of him at his new club. I'm just not sure he's the difference maker they think he is.

An (existing and competing) expansion club
At what point do we stop referring to Gold Coast and GWS as expansion clubs? Probably now. But I'm lumping them together in here for different reasons. The Suns were a total shambles this year, falling from flag favourite after three rounds to finishing in the bottom six and winning just two games after the mid-season byes. Spearhead Ben King has now departed the club and rumour has it Matt Rowell wants to follow suit. Damien Hardwick is under the pump and must show something in year four at the helm. Meanwhile, the Giants just held a fire sale, clearing out Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs. It's a bold move, and while it could pay dividends down the track, you figure there simply has to be some short term pain.

Those I WOULD want to be this AFL offseason
Zach Merrett
This time last year Merrett would have been top of my other list, but the veteran midfielder's wish of a fresh start at a new club has now been granted, and that must feel like an enormous weight has been lifted from his shoulders. Merrett joins the Hawks, a club which could easily have won the premiership this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's late heroics during preliminary final weekend. It means that for the first time in Merrett's career he will enter a season truly believing his side can go all the way. That's got to be a great feeling for an elite player who has toiled away for so long and enjoyed little success.

Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera
As we've established, his coach might be under immense pressure, but Wanganeen-Milera certainly shouldn't be feeling the pinch. In fact, he goes into next season with all options and possibilities on the table. If the Saints turn out to make good on their promise from last year and actually show they can compete with those at the pointy end, then he may well elect to sign on and remain at the club. But if 2027 turns out to be more of the same, he will have his choice of 17 new destinations to call home, including the two clubs from his home state of South Australia. Make no mistake, Wanganeen-Milera will be both the most discussed and in-demand player in the sport next season.

Andrew Mackie and Geelong's entire recruitment staff
When the siren sounded on the trade and free agency period, Geelong list boss Andrew Mackie should have been pumping his fists and popping bottles of champagne in celebration. The Cats have been arguably the biggest winners of the offseason to date, improving across every line with additions of former Giants captain Toby Greene, reliable ruck Rowan Marshall, and still criminally underrated key defender Jordan Ridley. It's a hefty haul and a great salvage after the club discovered at the eleventh hour it would be missing out on the services of Zak Butters. Mackie and his team have done their job, now it's over to Chris Scott and the playing group.

Fremantle fans
Alright, so there are the obvious reasons why you wouldn't want to be a Fremantle fan this offseason, but there are also plenty of reasons why you absolutely would. The Dockers came within an inch of winning their first premiership last month and proved to the footy world, and their supporters, the club has a list to not only go all the way in 2027 but remain one of the premier sides in the league for the next half decade. Just about everyone on this Fremantle squad is yet to hit their prime and has serious scope to improve next year. That should be both a worrying thought for the other 17 clubs and a great comfort to those who cheer for the men in purple.

Jason Horne-Francis
The departure of superstar midfielder Zak Butters during free agency means the keys to Port Adelaide now firmly belong to Horne-Francis. Some might argue he's shared those keys with Butters in recent years, but there's simply no denying who will be top dog at Port heading into next season. Horne-Francis is still just 23 years of age but he has shown he possesses all of the attributes to succeed as his club's main man. I expect him to relish the extra responsibility, too, and take his game to even greater heights. Jason, train hard and we'll see you in 2027!

Jaymie Graham
It must feel pretty special knowing a club made the decision to part ways with a four-time premiership-winning coach in favour of you, despite the fact you've never coached a senior AFL game. Graham arrives at Arden Street with an impressive resume as an assistant and has been tasked with ending North Melbourne's decade-long finals drought. Some will make the case he faces similar pressure to whoever takes over from Fagan at the Lions, but I see his role, at least in the immediate future, as one which carries far less of a burden. Given North's recent struggles, he will be offered (a little) time to get things right. His team is also in the sweet spot of being enough to win with now but not good enough to carry crazy expectation.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cochrane set for Ipswich Jets; Samrani to test open market
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Samrani expected to test open market
Jordan Samrani is expected to test the open market from November 1. ESPN understands he will explore his options for 2028 and beyond.

Following a breakout season with the Parramatta Eels, Samrani is open to assessing opportunities elsewhere when the contracting window opens on Sunday.

Cochrane set to link up with Titans feeder

Taye Cochrane is set to link up with Gold Coast Titans feeder club Ipswich Jets for the 2027 season following his departure from Canterbury.

ESPN understands the young fullback has signed with the Queensland Cup outfit after the Bulldogs opted against offering him a contract for next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances for Canterbury in 2026, having been part of the club's Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side in 2024.

The move follows Phil Gould's confirmation that Cochrane would leave the Bulldogs, with ESPN revealing he had not been offered a new deal.

Bulldogs opt against Cochrane deal

Canterbury have opted against offering Taye Cochrane a contract for 2027, with the young fullback set to depart Belmore.

ESPN understands Cochrane was not offered a new deal, following Phil Gould's confirmation he would not remain at the Bulldogs next season.

Cochrane scored six tries in 14 NSW Cup appearances this year, playing predominantly at fullback.

He was part of Canterbury's 2024 Jersey Flegg premiership-winning side before progressing to NSW Cup the following season.

Panthers make retention intentions clear on Patea
Penrith have informed Luron Patea's management of their desire to retain the young prop beyond 2027, although he still intends to test the open market from November 1.

ESPN understands multiple clubs are interested in speaking to Patea, who is approaching the final year of his Panthers contract.

ESPN previously reported that Penrith had yet to begin extension discussions with Patea.

Tigers keen to retain Mason

Wests Tigers are keen to retain Heath Mason, with the club working through roster space to accommodate the young utility.

ESPN understands Mason remains part of the Tigers' long-term plans, although his future is yet to be resolved ahead of 2027.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley says hamstring 'great' in return, not sweating back issue
stories.summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said his "hamstring came out great" and doesn't believe his back issue will keep him out after a gutsy and highly efficient performance in a loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said his "hamstring came out great" and doesn't believe his back issue will keep him out after a gutsy and highly efficient performance in Philadelphia's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night.

Barkley was questionable entering the game because of a hamstring injury that sidelined him the previous two weeks. The Eagles tried to limit his carries, and that number dropped further when his back locked up as the game progressed.

He played a total of nine snaps and touched the ball every time he was on the field, finishing with seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown, and two receptions for 9 yards.

Barkley is the first NFL starter in the past 20 seasons to play at least nine offensive snaps in a game and get a touch on all of them.

"When you go into something like that, you make sure the player's health is first and foremost," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. "Do they feel ready to go? Do the doctors and trainers feel like he's ready to go? And we felt like that was the case today. But obviously wanted to keep a close eye on him.

"He's tough as heck. He wanted to be out there for his teammates, probably had to slow him up. He'd be out there every play because of the person he is and the teammate he is and the toughness that he has."

Barkley was clearly managing the injuries throughout the game. He spent some time in the medical tent, and at one point, he stretched with trainers on the bench. Immediately following his 8-yard touchdown run on the first offensive possession, Barkley quickly made his way off the field and to the exercise bike on the sideline.

He tweaked his back on a 29-yard run in the first quarter and it got progressively worse from there, he said. His last snap of the game came in the third quarter.

Barkley said he didn't think the back issue would keep him out going forward but deferred to the training staff.

"It's kind of the school of thought I come from: I truly love this game, and I feel like if you're able to go, sometimes you've got to push your body to the limit," he said. "I'm trying, it's just not responding the way I want it to respond right now. It sucks because I'm trying to be the best leader I can be, and it's hard when you're not able to be out there and perform for your team."

The Eagles have gotten hit hard by injuries at running back. Will Shipley (foot), Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Carson Steele (shoulder) are on injured reserve. Dameon Pierce exited in the fourth quarter because of an undisclosed injury, leaving the running duties to Elijah Mitchell, who was brought up from the practice squad for the game.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: Harry Kane thanks Tottenham, pays tribute to England after Ballon d'Or win
stories.summary: Harry Kane thanked Tottenham for helping him fulfil his dreams and paid tribute to his international teammates after becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.
stories.body:
Harry Kane thanked Tottenham for helping him fulfil his dreams and paid tribute to his international teammates after becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.

The Bayern Munich striker beat Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to football's most prestigious individual award at a ceremony in London on Monday, becoming the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane, who joined Tottenham at the age of 11 before leaving for Bayern in 2023, reserved a special mention for his former club during his acceptance speech.

"I want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur. I wouldn't be where I am today without Tottenham, for sure," Kane said.

"I was there from 11 years old. [With] all the guidance, the coaches, you allowed me to live my dream.

"So, for sure, without all those moments together, all the ups and downs along the way of that journey has led me to this moment here today. So I just want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur."

Kane then singled out several coaches who helped him during his time at Spurs, including Chris Ramsey, Tim Sherwood and Ryan Mason, whom he described as one of his best friends.

The 33-year-old, who captained England to third place at the 2026 World Cup, also had praise for his international teammates during a lengthy and emotional speech.

"To all my England teammates. We had a special year," Kane said. "It wasn't the perfect year but we had a lot of good moments.

"We built a great bond together, a lot of togetherness, the way we played and it is truly an honour to play and captain you.

"This one is for all of us, for sure."

- Ballon d'Or 2026 results: Full rankings, all award winners

- Ballon d'Or site names Kane, Yamal and Mbappé as winners in blunder

- Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or

He added on coach Thomas Tuchel: "To Thomas Tuchel and the staff, the leadership, the way you drive us, the way you push standards, it is an honour to represent you."

Tuchel, meanwhile, congratulated his captain on becoming just the fifth Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or.

"Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon d'Or!" Tuchel said.

"I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

"To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.

"I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best -- scoring goals and winning football matches."

Wembley lit up its gold arches afterwards to mark Kane's historic achievement.

Kane, who also thanked several other coaches and Bayern -- including mentioning manager Vincent Kompany who is currently recovering from a collapse suffered last week -- finished off by saying: "To my wife Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs. You are my biggest support and I felt like you wanted this more than me.

"The anxious wait ... Here it is, we done it and you always want the best for me. You sacrifice yourself to make me achieve my dreams. This wouldn't be possible without you and it is something we can celebrate, not me. We're a team. I can't wait to celebrate tonight. I love you.

"My kids, sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime! To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry, you are the reason I do it. This is a special one and I can't wait to bring this home and celebrate with you. I love you very much."

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.body:

With the continuing growth of International Rugby League and the improving strength of the island nations, each World Cup throws up a tougher challenge.
